The facts of the prosecution case in brief are that, the accused and the deceased were neighbours and they both belong to same native village.
The accused and the deceased loved each other and the family of the deceased was against their marriage, as they were distant cousins in the relation.
In September 2022, the deceased had eloped with the accused and her mother lodged a missing complaint.
Later on, it was revealed that the accused and the deceased solemnised court marriage at Ghaziabad.
The deceased herself informed her mother about the marriage and mislead her about her location.

The complainant came to know that the accused and the SC No. 351/2023 FIR No. 250/2023 State v. Harsh Page 5 of 26  deceased started residing on rent at Tuglakabad and thereafter, they got shifted to Devli.
The deceased on telephone told her mother that the accused used to beat her and did not provide food.
The deceased told her mother that being harassed by the accused, she wanted to return back to her parental house but he did not allow her under threat either to commit suicide or to kill her.
2(B). On 31.12.2022, the deceased came to Saket Metro Station in order to come to the house of her sister Aarti but the accused stopped her under threat to commit suicide.
The accused stated to have convinced the deceased not to visit her sister's house on the pretext to go to the police station to resolve their dispute.
Instead of going to the police station, the accused took her back to the room and there he had beaten her and locked inside the room.
The accused used to confine the deceased inside the room and all these details were shared by the deceased with her sister Aarti.
The deceased told Aarti being disturbed and asked for work of domestic help.

STATUTORY PROVISIONS 09.

The charge has been framed against the accused for the commission of offences punishable under Section 498A/342/506 Part-II/306 IPC.
498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.

- Whoever , being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

- For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or State vs Harsh on 6 September, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45918043/
8

(b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand fro any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
306 IPC. Abetment of suicide.

- If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a terms which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

107 IPC defines abetment and it read as follows:
107. Abetment of a thing.-- A person abets the doing of a thing, who-- First. -- Instigates any person to do that thing; or Secondly.

-- Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing, if an act or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy, and in order to the doing of that thing; or Thirdly.

--
Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.

Explanation 1.-- A person who, by wilful misrepresentation, or by wilful concealment of a material fact which he is bound to disclose, voluntarily causes or procures, or attempts to cause or procure, a thing to be done, is said to instigate the doing of that thing.

Explanation 2.-- Whoever, either prior to or at the time of the commission of an act, does anything in order to facilitate the commission of that act, and thereby facilitate the commission thereof, is said to aid the doing of that act.

She must be subjected to cruelty or harassment; iii. Such cruelty or harassment must have been done either by husband of the woman or by the relative of her husband.
13. The cruelty as defined under Section 498A IPC may be physical or mental.
It is a settled preposition of law that every kind of harassment would not amount to cruelty within the meaning of provisions of Section 498A IPC.
Every case has to be analysed individually to assess whether the act of the accused would amount to cruelty.

On perusal of the statutory provision, it is clear that, the cruelty simplicitor is not sufficient to constitute the offence, rather it must be done either with intention to cause grave injury or to drive her to commit suicide or with intention to coerce her meet unlawful demands.

Reliance is placed upon the judgement of the Apex Court in the case titled and reported as Kamlakar v. state of Karnataka Crl. No. 1485/2011 (decided on 12.10.2023); 2023 INSC 989;

sentences.text: "8.2. Section 306 IPC penalizes abetment of commission of suicide.
To charge someone under this Section, the prosecution must prove that the accused played a role in the suicide.
Specifically, the accused's actions must align with one of the three criteria detailed in Section 107 IPC.

This means the accused either encouraged the individual to take their life, conspired with others to ensure the person committed suicide, or acted in a way (or failed to act) which directly resulted in the person's suicide.
8.3. In Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chattishgarh, this Court has analysed different meanings of "instigation".

entities.text: Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chattishgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant para of the said judgement is reproduced herein:

"20. Instigation is to goad, urge forward, provoke, incite or encourage to do "an act".
To satisfy the requirement of instigation though it is not necessary that actual words must be used to that effect or what constitutes instigation must necessarily and specifically be suggestive of the consequence.
Yet a reasonable certainty to incite the consequence must be capable of being spelt out.
